section: Satavahana administration, economy, coinage and Prakrit literature (Hala's Gathasaptasati)

accepted.s: In the Satavahana administrative system, the term ‘Raja’ denoted which of the following?
o: A military officer supervising temporary camps
The highest feudatory who could issue coins
A village assembly dealing with local administration
A minister responsible for royal revenue
accepted.x: Raja was the highest-ranking feudatory in the Satavahana polity and possessed the authority to issue coins.
accepted.tq: Test the exact administrative meaning of a title rather than confusing it with a royal office.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: A Mahabhoja was a powerful local feudatory chief. Maharathi was a feudatory title, Senapati was a military chief, and Gaulmika was associated with rural administration.
accepted.tq: Use the person-title and office-meaning distinction to eliminate swapped administrative roles.

accepted.s: Naganika, associated with the Satavahana period, was the daughter of a person holding which title?
accepted.x: Naganika was the daughter of a Maharathi, a feudatory title in the Satavahana polity.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct title through the kinship association given in the historical record.

accepted.s: The officer who administered regions and was responsible for the day-to-day military affairs of the Satavahana kingdom was the
accepted.x: The Mahasenapati was the military chief who handled the day-to-day military administration of regions. The king remained the supreme commander.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the supreme commander from the officer handling routine military affairs.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Satavahana military and administrative centres is correct?
o: Skandhavara was a city assembly, whereas Kataka denoted land revenue.
Kataka was a temporary campaign camp, whereas Skandhavara was a permanent garrison.
Kataka was a permanent military camp or fortified administrative centre, whereas Skandhavara was a temporary campaign camp.
Both Kataka and Skandhavara referred exclusively to tax-free villages granted to Brahmanas.
accepted.x: Kataka denoted a permanent military camp, garrison or fortified administrative centre, generally located in cities. Skandhavara was a temporary military camp used during campaigns.
accepted.tq: Separate the two look-alike military terms by permanence and purpose.

accepted.s: The land revenue known as ‘Bhaga’ under the Satavahanas was generally fixed at
accepted.x: Bhaga was the land revenue collected at one-sixth of the produce.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact revenue fraction and distinguish it from nearby agrarian shares.

accepted.s: According to Pliny, the Satavahana army consisted of
accepted.x: Pliny mentions 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants in the Satavahana army.
accepted.tq: Match each numerical component with the correct military category instead of relying on the total alone.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the military organisation of the Satavahanas?
o: The army consisted only of infantry and cavalry, without elephants or archers.
The Chaturanga bala comprised chariots, elephants, cavalry and infantry, and archers also formed part of the military arrangement.
The king was not connected with military command, which was vested entirely in feudatories.
Archers were placed in front, while infantry was always stationed at the rear.
accepted.x: The Satavahana army was described as Chaturanga bala—chariots, elephants, cavalry and infantry—with archers also present. The king was the supreme commander.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute exclusions and identify the complete composition of the fourfold army.

accepted.s: According to the arrangement depicted in Amaravati sculptures, which sequence correctly represents the deployment of Satavahana forces?
o: Infantry in front, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, archers at the rear
Cavalry in front, infantry on the flanks, elephants at the rear
Elephants in front, archers on the flanks, cavalry at the rear
Archers in front, elephants at the rear, infantry on the flanks
accepted.x: Amaravati sculptures show infantry in front, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, and archers at the rear.
accepted.tq: Reconstruct the battlefield arrangement by fixing the front and rear positions first.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the political structure of the Satavahana kingdom?
o: It was semi-feudal, and the king upheld the Dharmashastras.
It was completely centralised and had no feudatory elements.
It was a republican confederation governed by town assemblies.
It was governed exclusively by Buddhist monastic authorities.
accepted.x: The Satavahana polity was semi-feudal, and the king was expected to uphold the Dharmashastras.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the broad character of the polity from the administrative institutions functioning within it.

accepted.s: Which language was associated with the speech of common people during the Satavahana period?
accepted.x: The common people spoke Desi bhasha, while Prakrit served as the royal, administrative and inscriptional language.
accepted.tq: Separate the language of popular speech from the official and inscriptional language.

accepted.s: Who is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language during the Satavahana period?
accepted.x: Kuntala Satakarni, regarded as the thirteenth Satavahana king, is associated with making Sanskrit the royal language.
accepted.tq: Match the language policy with the specific ruler rather than with a better-known Satavahana king.

accepted.s:
With reference to the development of Sanskrit and Telugu in the Deccan, consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus.
2. The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman is regarded as the first complete Sanskrit inscription.
3. ‘Nagabu’ is identified as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.
4. ‘Vepuru’ occurs in the Myakadoni inscription.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus; Rudradaman’s Junagadh inscription is the first complete Sanskrit inscription, while Nagabu and Vepuru occur in the Amaravati and Myakadoni inscriptions respectively.
accepted.tq: Track the ruler, inscription and word-location pairs separately before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: ‘Nagabu’ is identified as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription. ‘Vepuru’ appears in the Myakadoni inscription, while the Junagadh inscription is associated with Sanskrit.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar inscriptional evidence by matching each word with its location.

accepted.s: The Satavahanas are regarded as the first rulers in India to provide tax-free land grants to
accepted.x: The Satavahanas made tax-free grants of villages or land to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks. This practice later contributed to the early-medieval feudal order.
accepted.tq: Recall the recipients of the earliest tax-free grants without extending the grant to unrelated groups.

accepted.s: The Satavahana practice of granting tax-free villages to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks later became a basis for the development of
o: The urban guild system of the Mauryas
accepted.x: Tax-free land grants created rights and immunities that later formed a basis of the early-medieval feudal order.
accepted.tq: Identify the historical consequence of an institutional practice rather than its immediate recipients.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Satakarni I and Gautamiputra Satakarni is correct?
o: Satakarni I granted land, cows and gold to Brahmanas at Naneghat, while Gautamiputra granted a village at Tirasmri to monks and 100 nivartanas of his own land.
Satakarni I granted Tirasmri to monks, while Gautamiputra made the Naneghat donation to Brahmanas.
Both rulers granted only military camps and imposed taxes on the recipients.
Neither ruler is associated with land grants to religious beneficiaries.
accepted.x: At Naneghat, Satakarni I gave land, cows or godhana, and gold to Brahmanas. Gautamiputra gave the village of Tirasmri to monks along with 100 nivartanas of his own land.
accepted.tq: Compare two rulers by separating the place, beneficiaries and contents of their grants.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT an immunity associated with Gautamiputra’s Nasik grants?
o: The grantees were required to provide unlimited military service to royal officers.
Royal officers and soldiers were prohibited from entering the granted area.
The grant was free from district police and royal dues.
accepted.x: The Nasik grants provided immunities from entry by royal officers and soldiers, salt-digging, district police and royal dues. They did not impose unlimited military service on the grantees.
accepted.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated set of fiscal and administrative immunities.
